p: The Centre will form a high-level committee to settle water sharing between Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka on the Tungabhadra.
Friction points: Karnataka's Upper Bhadra project (upstream) worries the downstream States, and Telangana is not getting its share through the silted Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme.
Constitution: water is a State subject (List II), but the Union can regulate inter-State rivers (List I). Article 262 lets Parliament set up tribunals and bar courts from hearing such disputes.

Two laws follow from this: the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 (ad-hoc tribunals; 2002 amendment: tribunal within 1 year, award within 3) and the River Boards Act 1956 (no board ever formed).

Courts still step in through Article 131 (original jurisdiction) and Article 136 (appeals). The 2018 Cauvery verdict modified the award and ordered a Cauvery Management Board. Dam safety (Mullaperiyar) is not a 'water dispute' under the Act.
Problems: delays in forming tribunals and notifying awards, no enforcement powers, weak data, and little stakeholder consultation (Narmada).
Fixes: the 2019 Amendment Bill (one permanent tribunal plus a dispute resolution committee), Inter-State Council (Article 263), a national water data bank and whole-basin management.
Both follow the Westminster model: a nominal head of state, a real executive led by the PM drawn from the legislature, two Houses, and collective responsibility to the lower House.
UK has parliamentary sovereignty and an unwritten constitution; India has constitutional supremacy and a written one.
Judicial review: Indian courts can strike down laws; UK courts cannot invalidate Acts of Parliament.
In India a minister can sit for six months without being an MP; the UK PM is traditionally an MP in the Commons.
India has an anti-defection law; the UK has none.
NeSDA is a two-yearly assessment by DARPG of how well States, UTs, cities and Central Ministries deliver online services.
It borrows its method from the Online Service Index of the UN e-Government Survey.
It checks availability, accessibility and maturity of services, looking at government-to-citizen and government-to-business services.
Portals are grouped as general portals and service portals.
A Central Sector Scheme of the Department of Justice for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, built on the earlier DISHA scheme (2021-26) which reached over 2.37 crore people.
Tele-Law gives free pre-litigation advice through about 2.5 lakh Common Service Centres.
Nyaya Bandhu links poor and marginalised people (eligible under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987) with pro bono lawyers.
Legal literacy and awareness programmes work with ministries and civil society.
VIDHI-Sanjeevani is the new digital platform to track the whole programme with data.

topics.t: Right to trauma care, right to be forgotten, right to walk
p: Trauma care: in SaveLIFE Foundation the Supreme Court read it into Article 21 and asked for one emergency number (112), cashless treatment under PM RAHAT and a grievance system for Good Samaritans.
Why it matters: about 4.67 lakh accidental deaths a year; nearly half of road deaths could be prevented with timely care.

Right to be forgotten: the Delhi High Court called it part of privacy under Article 21. Names can be de-indexed (removed from name searches, record kept) or masked (shown as XYZ), mostly in acquittals; not for cases involving women, children or breach of public trust.
Right to walk: the Supreme Court held that safe, marked footpaths are a Fundamental Right, flowing from Article 19(1)(d) (movement) and Article 21 (life with dignity).

topics.t: Proof of citizenship and FCRA rules
p: MEA says a passport is a travel document, not conclusive proof of citizenship. Section 20 of the Passports Act lets the Centre issue passports to non-citizens in public interest.

No single document proves citizenship: Aadhaar is identity only; the electoral roll gives a presumption, not proof (Lal Babu Hussein, 1995); citizenship certificates are issued mainly to those who got citizenship by registration or naturalisation.

FCRA 2010 controls foreign money and hospitality for NGOs and individuals, to protect sovereignty and public interest. The 2020 amendment banned sub-granting, capped admin costs at 20% and required an SBI account.
Proposed new rules: funds only for approved activities, NGOs only in declared States, disclosure of social media and key people, religious activity allowed but conversion activity barred.

topics.t: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (COSP19)
p: The 19th Conference of States Parties met in New York, marking 20 years of the Convention under the theme 'CRPD at 20'.
The Convention (UNGA 2006, in force 2008) is a binding human rights treaty built on a rights-based, social model of disability.
India ratified it in October 2007 and implemented it through the RPwD Act 2016, which raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21; Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan promotes accessibility.
Its monitoring body is the CRPD Committee; an Optional Protocol allows individual complaints.
The 11th Quad foreign ministers' meeting was held in New Delhi.

Outcomes: undersea cable links for Pacific Island Forum countries by 2026, ports support in Fiji, a Maritime Surveillance Collaboration initiative, a 20 billion dollar Critical Minerals framework and an energy security initiative, plus 6G standards cooperation.
India will host the next Coast Guard-led Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission after the first one (Palau to Guam).

Quad is an informal grouping of India, US, Japan and Australia, rooted in 2004 tsunami relief, proposed by Abe in 2007 and revived in 2017. Malabar involves all four navies but is not formally a Quad exercise.
Why India cares: critical minerals, maritime security, digital connectivity, energy and disaster relief.
Weak spots: differing priorities, no secretariat or funding, slow delivery, the US renaming Indo-Pacific Command back to Pacific Command, and AUKUS.
India chairs BRICS in 2026. The 16th agriculture ministers' meeting at Indore was the first to include partner countries.
The Indore Declaration covers food security, farmer welfare, climate-resilient farming, trade and digital agriculture.

New bodies: a Global Forum on Farmers' Rights in Seed Systems (run via PPV&FR Authority), BRICS AGRIN for seeds and inputs, a Network of Centres of Excellence on agroecology (ICAR-IIFSR) and a Network on Digital Agriculture (IIT Delhi).
GIAHS (an FAO heritage-farming label): India has Kuttanad, Koraput and Pampore saffron.

BRICS basics: acronym by Jim O'Neill (2001); NDB set up at Fortaleza 2014 (100 billion dollars, Shanghai) plus a 100 billion dollar Contingent Reserve Arrangement; no permanent secretariat; new members include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE and Indonesia; Saudi Arabia undecided.
India's challenges: keeping BRICS non-western rather than anti-western, China's dominance and divisions such as Iran-UAE.
Adopted on 14 June 2026 during the PM's visit to Nice, tied to the 2026 India-France Year of Innovation and the Horizon 2047 roadmap.
Aim: move from buyer-seller to co-design, co-development and co-production, and lean on India's software talent plus France's hardware strength.

Four pillars: trusted AI (governance, child safety, data sharing linking DEPA with French data spaces); academic mobility (30,000 Indian students in France by 2030, wider qualification recognition); technological sovereignty and industry-academia links (startup corridor, Kanpur aeronautics campus, space events); AI for global health (ICMR with France's Health Data Hub).
Hurdles: France's NATO alignment versus India's non-alignment, and EU regulations while trade lags defence.

topics.t: G7 summit, India-US and India-UK minerals, Myanmar, Oman, Venezuela
p: G7 at Evian, France: India attended as a partner; the PM said the world has a 'shortage of trust' and called for partnerships based on equality.

India-US framework on critical minerals and rare earths (building on Pax Silica and FORGE) targets financing, recycling and supply diversification. China holds about 49% of rare earth reserves, 69% of output and 90% of processing.
India-UK Critical Minerals Observatory (TEXMiN, IIT-ISM Dhanbad, Cambridge) will track global supply chains and support the National Critical Mineral Mission.
India-Myanmar: Rupee-Kyat settlement since 2024; Kaladan project and trilateral highway; 1,643 km border; shared Theravada heritage.
India-Oman CEPA is in force: 99.38% of India's exports get zero duty in Oman; India opens 77.79% of tariff lines while protecting dairy, oilseeds and cereals.
India-Venezuela: trade of 678.94 million dollars; Venezuela became India's 3rd largest oil supplier in May 2026.

topics.t: IMEC, CPEC, Global Alliance for Human Rights, Global Peace Index, border items
p: IMEC (announced at G20 2023): an East corridor to the Gulf and a North corridor to Europe; expected to cut transit time 40% and costs 30%. The Iran-Israel conflict and Hormuz disruption threaten it.
CPEC (BRI flagship, Gwadar to Kashgar) is being upgraded to CPEC 2.0; India opposes it because it crosses Indian territory under illegal occupation.
OHCHR's Global Alliance for Human Rights leads up to the 80th anniversary of the UDHR in 2028; guiding words: Imagine, Dialogue, Act.
Global Peace Index 2026: India 127th of 163; Iceland first for the 19th year; Russia last.
Bangladesh approved the Padma barrage as the 1996 Ganga water treaty nears its December 2026 expiry.
India-China trade via Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) resumes after 6 years; other trade passes are Shipki La and Nathu La.
The middle class is growing with higher incomes and urbanisation; the WEF expects the middle class and affluent to make up 93% of spending by 2036 (80% in 2026).
Private consumption is projected to grow 7% and reach 61.5% of GDP, the highest since FY12; 93% of urban consumer growth is expected outside the top five cities.

Worries: GNI per capita is about 2,600 dollars against the 4,500 needed for upper-middle-income status; household debt at 45.5% of GDP; the top 10% own about 65% of wealth; AI could cut 1.5 million tech jobs by 2031; low women's workforce participation.

Support so far: no tax up to Rs 12 lakh (Budget 2025-26), the Unified Pension Scheme, MUDRA loans (57 crore, Rs 40.07 lakh crore), SWAMIH fund for stalled housing, and Ayushman Vay Vandana cards for 70+.
Way ahead: manufacturing push (PLI, National Manufacturing Mission), AI skills, curbing household debt, more women at work and price stability.

The government is making G-Secs easier for foreign portfolio investors: tax exemptions on interest and capital gains, more securities under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR), and a higher equity limit for non-resident individuals (10% to 24%).
G-Secs are tradeable debt of the Centre or States, sold through RBI auctions on the E-Kuber platform, with practically no default risk.

Types: Treasury bills (91, 182, 364 days; zero-coupon, issued at a discount), Cash Management Bills (under 91 days, since 2010), dated securities (coupon every six months, 1 to 40 years) and State Development Loans (States issue only these).
Risks to a holder: market risk, reinvestment risk and liquidity risk.
FPI is passive and short-term; FDI brings management control and is long-term.

topics.t: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code at 10 years
p: The IBC (2016, from the T.K. Viswanathan committee) unified insolvency law and moved from 'debtor in possession' to a time-bound, creditor-in-control model; the IBC Amendment Act 2026 was notified.

Process: the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, with a Committee of Creditors of financial creditors judging resolution plans; pre-packaged insolvency for MSMEs within 120 days; IBBI is the regulator.

Results: bank gross NPAs fell from 11.5% (FY18) to 2.3% (FY26); over Rs 4 lakh crore recovered, about 170% of liquidation value; 30,000+ cases worth about Rs 13.78 lakh crore settled before admission.

Problems: cases take about 744 days against the 330-day limit; big haircuts; clogged NCLTs; the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Fund is not operational; ED attachments under PMLA clash with the clean-slate principle.

The 2026 Act adds a creditor-initiated out-of-court process, a 14-day admission deadline, liquidation in 180 days (plus up to 90), a cross-border and group insolvency framework, creditor oversight of liquidation and a firm clean slate.

The Supreme Court criticised a bank-ARC-borrower nexus where loans are sold cheaply to ARCs and borrowers settle for a fraction; it said 'commercial wisdom' cannot excuse reckless waivers of public money.

ARCs buy bad loans from banks (idea from Narasimham Committee II, 1998). They are registered with the RBI under Section 3 of the SARFAESI Act 2002. ARCIL (2002) was the first; there are 27 now, plus the government-backed NARCL.
Payment is mostly in Security Receipts that pay out only when the ARC recovers the loan; ARCs charge 1.5-2% yearly and must hold 15% of the receipts.
RBI Directions 2025: minimum net owned fund Rs 300 crore, capital adequacy 15%, no deposits, resolve assets in 5 years (up to 8), CEO age cap 70.
Weaknesses: recovery of only 15-20% of book value, conflicts in roles, 80% of recoveries through enforcement rather than revival, and a loophole letting promoters buy back their own bad assets.
Sudarshan Sen Committee (2021): let ARCs sponsor AIFs and buy early-stress (SMA) accounts.
The Logistics Port Performance Index (LPPI) FY2024-25 under Sagar Aankalan benchmarks ports on dry bulk, liquid bulk and containers: Paradip, Sikka and Mundra topped.

Four digital tools from the Directorate General of Shipping: e-Navik grievance system for seafarers, digital ship registration on e-Samudra, a doctor module to stop fake seafarer certificates, and a ship recycling portal.

Facts: 11,099 km coast; 12 major ports; 95% of trade volume, 70% of value; second-largest seafarer supplier (12.16%); largest ship recycler (35.4% of world, Alang about 98% of India's). The Hong Kong Convention on ship recycling came into force on 26 June 2025.
Weakness: shipbuilding is only about 0.06% of the world market, and about 75% of transhipment cargo is handled abroad (Vizhinjam is the answer being built).

Push: Maritime India Vision 2030 and Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (5% of shipbuilding by 2030), Rs 25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund, Rs 24,736 crore shipbuilding financial assistance, Rs 19,989 crore Shipbuilding Development Scheme, new shipping laws of 2025 and the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme.

topics.t: PMKVY and the Public Accounts Committee
p: PAC flagged weak results in the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (2015; run through NSDC, a 49:51 government-private company).
Targets missed: 1.10 crore certified against 1.32 crore; only 41% placed; of Rs 14,449 crore outlay, Rs 10,194 crore released and Rs 9,261 crore used.
Data and monitoring gaps: invalid bank details for 90.66 lakh of 95.90 lakh participants, biometric attendance missing in recognition of prior learning, unreliable documents.
Training was pointed at low-demand sectors such as apparel, electronics and retail, with no national skill plan.
Advice: align with local demand, finish the National Skill Development Plan, merge skilling schemes and improve IT controls.
The Ministry of Tourism and NITI Aayog report 'Unlocking Growth in Tourism and Hospitality' (2026) seeks simpler rules and more investment.
India is 39th of 119 on the WEF tourism index; tourism gave 5.22% of GDP and about 13.3% of jobs; target of 100 million inbound visitors and a 3 trillion dollar sector by 2047.
Obstacles: a hotel needs about 50 approvals and takes 36-48 months to open; limited visa-on-arrival; Visa Openness Index 38.14; India has under 1.5% of world arrivals.
Schemes: Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, SASCI (Rs 3,295.76 crore for 40 sites), Cruise Bharat Mission (51 circuits), Vibrant Villages and Dekho Apna Desh.
Fixes: 90-day multiple-entry visa on arrival, self-declaration for hotel grading, a National Institute of Hospitality and sustainability tools such as Travel for LiFE.

topics.t: ILO platform work convention and State finances
p: ILO Convention No. 193 (114th session) is the first binding global standard for gig and platform workers: correct classification, minimum wage where they are employees, social security, safety, algorithm transparency and human review of automated decisions. It starts 12 months after two ratifications.
ILO: set up in 1919, UN's first specialised agency (1946), Nobel Peace Prize 1969; India has ratified six of the eight core conventions (not Nos. 87 and 98 on association and collective bargaining).

CAG on State finances 2024-25: combined public debt Rs 75.52 lakh crore (23.27% of GSDP); 18 States above the 3% fiscal deficit limit; capital spending only 16.59% of expenditure; States' share of Union taxes rose from 27.73% to 31.76%.
Subsidies stayed at 8-10% of States' revenue spending, mostly for power utilities and agriculture.

topics.t: Statistics and global outlook: WPI, DDP, World Bank, unicorns
p: New Wholesale Price Index (base 2022-23): 957 items, manufactured goods weigh most; first Producer Price Indices and a service PPI for seven services launched, with PPI set to replace WPI in five years.
District Domestic Product guidelines (base 2022-23) give district-level GDP and per capita income.
World Bank approved a 1.5 billion dollar Development Policy Financing loan for India.
Global Economic Prospects 2026: world growth slips from 2.9% to 2.5% because of the Iran conflict and Hormuz disruption; South Asia still fastest but moderating from 7.0% to 6.3%.
Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026: India has 61 unicorns, 4th place; Bengaluru has 25.

SARTHAK-PDS merges the foodgrain transport/dealer margin scheme and SMART PDS: Rs 25,530 crore until March 2031 for about 81.35 crore NFSA beneficiaries. AAY families get 35 kg a month; priority households 5 kg per person.
Smart Warehousing: AI and IoT in 215 CWC warehouses (FCI adding 150), with FASTag gates, smart locks and fire/rodent detection.
Muga silk (Assam): the world's only naturally golden silk, India's first GI-tagged silk, 90% of world output; Mission Senehjori aims at 5 reeling units and 30 FPOs by 2028.

Queen Pineapple Mission (Tripura, MDoNER); pineapple is Tripura's State Fruit. National Seed Reserve of 1.74 lakh quintals uses the SATHI portal. BIS standard IS 20201:2026 covers community seed banks.
FAO SOFIA 2026: world output 235 million tonnes; India is 2nd with 9%, and 2nd in aquaculture with 12%.
RBI lets banks lend against FCNR(B) deposits (foreign-currency NRI term deposits of 1 to 5 years, fully repatriable) and lend directly to REITs and InvITs.
Zero Coupon Zero Principal bonds issued by non-profits on the Social Stock Exchange can now count for CSR, capped at 10% of a company's CSR spend.
TReDS lets MSMEs sell invoices for early payment; GeM has integrated it. CGSMFI-2.0 guarantees loans to microfinance institutions (80%, 75%, 70% by size).
NPCI's Drunix is an open-source blockchain framework re-engineered from Hyperledger Fabric.
Sagarmala Finance Corporation will issue India's first blue bonds (Seychelles issued the first sovereign blue bond in 2018).
A Rs 10,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund will smooth aviation fuel prices for 36 months; fuel is about 40% of airline costs.
DRDO showed multi-layer defence against long-range ballistic missiles and a medium-range anti-ship missile.
India's BMD programme began in 1999. Phase I covers threats up to 2,000 km; in June 2026 Phase II with AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors proved capability against 5,000 km-class missiles.
Phase III (AD-AH and AD-AM) is for hypersonic glide vehicles and MIRVs.
Range classes: short (<1,000 km, Prithvi-II), medium (Agni-II), intermediate (Agni-IV about 4,000 km), ICBM (>5,500 km, Agni-V).
NASM-MR is an indigenous, all-weather, over-the-horizon, sea-skimming cruise missile.
Why BMD matters: protects cities and command centres, keeps second-strike ability and buys decision time.
Minister Jitendra Singh said AI, quantum, biotech and space are reshaping national security.

Efforts: iDEX and ADITI (grants up to Rs 25 crore), National Quantum Mission, Military Quantum Mission policy 2026, drone roadmap, Defence AI Council and Project Agency, Defence Space Agency and Defence Cyber Agency.

Gaps: skills shortage, weak cyber law, unclear AI intellectual property, dependence on foreign platforms and embedded-malware risk, cancelled projects such as the Battlefield Management System and AI 'black box' opacity.
Way ahead: grow home-grown design capability, build civil-military research links, and adopt AI with ethical safeguards.

topics.t: Illegal immigration and demographic change committee
p: A high-level committee under Justice P.P. Navlekar (with the Census Commissioner) will study unnatural demographic change from illegal immigration and suggest a time-bound way to identify, detain and deport illegal migrants.

Law: the Citizenship Act 1955 defines an illegal migrant (no valid documents or overstaying). CAA 2019 exempts six communities from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh who entered before 31 December 2014. The Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025 punishes illegal entry with up to 5 years and Rs 5 lakh fine.
Problems: long, partly riverine borders (about 25% of the Bangladesh border cannot be fenced), forged papers, no refugee law (India is outside the 1951 Convention), no deportation authority.
Courts: Salimullah (2021) allowed Rohingya deportation only by due process; NHRC v Arunachal Pradesh (1996) said Article 21 protects foreigners from unlawful eviction.
Suggested: border technology, a central authority in MHA, bilateral repatriation deals and a national refugee law.

topics.t: SIPRI yearbook, Shangri-La Dialogue and defence news
p: SIPRI 2026: about 12,187 nuclear warheads; India about 190 (China 620, Pakistan 170); world military spending a record 2.9 trillion dollars; India 5th with 92.1 billion; India is the 2nd largest arms importer (about 8%).
India signed a BrahMos supply deal with Vietnam at the Shangri-La Dialogue (Singapore, run by IISS). BrahMos: Mach 2.8, 290 km.
DRDO's Netra AEW&C reached Final Operational Clearance; it uses AESA radar on an Embraer EMB-145I and made India the 5th country with home-built AEW&C.
RudraM-II air-to-surface missile tested; LRLACM (successor to Nirbhay, about 1,000 km) tested; Russia offered the Su-57 and joint production.
Exercises: PRAGATI (12 Indian Ocean partners) and Khaan Quest in Mongolia.
India's ABS system under the Biological Diversity Act 2002 has collected over Rs 266 crore and paid out about Rs 145 crore; Red Sanders gave 45% of it, seeds 32.3%, pharma and AYUSH 13.8%.

ABS means that when genetic resources or traditional knowledge are used commercially, the benefits are shared with the communities that preserved them. Its parent is the Nagoya Protocol (in force 2014) under the Convention on Biological Diversity.

Key ideas: state sovereignty over resources, Prior Informed Consent from the provider country, Mutually Agreed Terms, and the ABS Clearing-House (Article 14). The Cali Fund (from COP16) collects money for use of Digital Sequence Information.

India's three tiers: National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards and local Biodiversity Management Committees. The 2025 Regulations replaced the 2014 rules and bring in Digital Sequence Information and turnover-based benefit shares.

Examples: Jeevani drug and the Kani tribe (50% of fees shared), turmeric and neem patent revocations (first time a developing country's traditional knowledge patent was overturned), Divya Pharmacy 2018 judgment, PepsiCo seaweed sourcing in Tamil Nadu.
Related treaty: the FAO Plant Treaty (2001; 64 crops in a common pool, Benefit Sharing Fund 2009).

UNEP and the GEF launched a 23.5 million dollar programme (50 million co-finance) to check how well the Stockholm and Minamata conventions are working and to help poorer countries monitor hazardous chemicals.

Stockholm Convention (2001; in force 2004): bans or limits persistent organic pollutants such as DDT, aldrin and chlordane. India ratified in 2006 with the opt-out clause, so new additions don't bind it automatically.
Minamata Convention on Mercury (2013; in force 2017; India is a party): no new mercury mines, phase-out of mercury products and processes, control of emissions and of small-scale gold mining.

UNEP: set up in 1972, based in Nairobi, hosts the UN Environment Assembly (193 members). GEF: set up in 1991, the largest multilateral environment funder, with the World Bank as trustee; it serves six conventions including CBD, UNFCCC, Stockholm, Minamata, UNCCD and the BBNJ Agreement.

topics.t: Climate news: Bonn talks, carbon markets, methane, energy index
p: SB64 in Bonn prepares COP31 (Antalya, Turkiye, 9-20 November 2026). New 2035 goals: electricity at 35% of final energy, halve the growth in waste, cut building energy intensity by 25%.
India and Japan finalised a Joint Crediting Mechanism under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, India's first live bilateral carbon trading framework; the Delhi Metro qualifies.
WMO decadal update: 80% chance that some year in 2024-28 exceeds 1.5 degrees; 86% chance of a year hotter than 2023.
Turquoise Nexus Initiative (COP31 Presidency with FAO) puts food-water-climate links into national climate plans.
WEF Energy Transition Index 2026: readiness fell for the first time in over a decade; Sweden, Finland and Denmark lead; India rose two places to 70th.
UN Call to Action on Methane supports the Global Methane Pledge (cut 30% by 2030; India is not a signatory). Methane is about 80 times stronger than CO2 over 20 years but lasts only about a decade.

topics.t: Energy transition: floating solar, coal gasification, flex fuel, BESS, hydrogen
p: Floating solar potential is 102.18 GWp (Maharashtra leads); total assessed solar potential is 3,445 GWp; installed solar rose from 2.8 GW (2014) to 155 GW (2026).
India's first commercial coal-to-ammonium nitrate plant in Odisha (BHEL-Coal India joint venture, 2,000 tonnes a day); the National Coal Gasification Mission targets 100 million tonnes by 2030.
Flex-fuel cars run on E20 to E100; ethanol has lower energy density so mileage drops; concerns are food-versus-fuel and sugarcane water use. India may blend isobutanol with diesel.
Battery storage: the world's largest single-site BESS outside China (3.37 GWh, Khavda); target of 47 GW by 2032; viability gap funding for 4,000 MWh.
Green hydrogen: Rs 19,744 crore mission, definition of at most 2 kg CO2 per kg of H2, new certification portal and India's first hydrogen train from Jind.
Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal, Ballia, UP) became India's 100th Ramsar site: an oxbow lake of about 3,432 ha, a wintering ground on the Central Asian Flyway.

Species: albino hog deer in Kaziranga (Endangered, Schedule I); caracal sighted in Kuno; Tapanuli orangutan (Critically Endangered, only in Batang Toru, Sumatra) lost about 7% of its population in a 2025 cyclone.
Corals: ZSI picked four new sites to move corals and giant clams displaced by the Great Nicobar transhipment port; a giant Pavona clavus coral (about 4,250 sq m) was found at Kadmat, Lakshadweep.
Tamil Nadu will place India's first 3D-printed artificial reef (Tvasta with ICAR-CMFRI) under PMMSY.

A seismic doublet (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5) hit western Venezuela. Kishau dam (Tons river, 236 m) got a six-State MoU; Kirthai-II is the third new Chenab hydro project after the Indus Water Treaty suspension.
Young people across the world are leading leaderless, digitally organised protests: Sri Lanka 2022, Bangladesh 2024, Nepal, Indonesia, Madagascar 2025.
Causes: the largest-ever youth population (2.4 billion aged 10-29), inequality (richest 10% own 76% of wealth), youth unemployment of 13%, fear of AI taking entry-level jobs, and a need to belong.
India's Gen Z protests were different: they asked for specific accountability rather than regime change and relied on sit-ins, petitions and fasts (Sonam Wangchuk's 26-day fast).
Risks: capture by political or foreign interests and no leadership to negotiate after the protest.

Way ahead: quality jobs, trusted exam systems (National Recruitment Agency, Public Examinations Act 2024), grievance redress (CPGRAMS), skilling linked to jobs, real youth consultation and protest rules that respect Article 19.

topics.t: Digital health and universal health coverage
p: India has created over 90 crore ABHA health accounts and linked over 100 crore health records under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (2021).
Tools: telemedicine (eSanjeevani), Health Facility and Professionals Registries, U-WIN for vaccines, IHIP for disease surveillance, AI screening such as MadhuNetrAI.
Legal base: National Health Policy 2017, National Digital Health Blueprint 2019, Telemedicine Guidelines 2020 and the DPDP Act 2023.
Problems: weak rural internet, privacy risks, low digital skills, systems that don't talk to each other, and exclusion through failed Aadhaar authentication.
Fixes: more broadband, standard health records, stronger data governance and private sector participation.
NFHS-6 covered 6.79 lakh households in 715 districts (IIPS Mumbai nodal) and added new questions on DBT, SHGs, digital literacy and HIV testing.
Population and care: fertility steady at 2.0; institutional births 90.6%; health insurance cover 60.2% of households (from 41%); full vaccination 87.1%; rotavirus vaccine 85.4% (from 36.4%).
Nutrition: stunting down from 35.5% to 29.3%; severe wasting 7.7% to 5.2%; underweight hardly moved (31.8%).
Women: internet use 33.3% to 64.3%; own bank account 89%; spousal violence down to 22.3%; child marriage down to 20.1%.
Warning signs: C-sections up to 27.2%, women overweight 30.7%, men with high blood sugar 20.9%.

topics.t: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (10 years)
p: Free specialist check-ups for pregnant women (2nd and 3rd trimester) at public facilities on the 9th of every month; Extended PMSMA (Jan 2022) tracks high-risk pregnancies till 45 days after delivery.
Results: over 7.5 crore check-ups; maternal mortality fell from 130 (2014-16) to 87 (SRS 2022-24); India met the NHP 2017 goal of under 100, and eight States already meet the SDG goal of under 70.
Gaps: overloaded ASHAs, scarce obstetricians and sonologists, poor diagnostics, social barriers and little postnatal focus.
Fixes: link records with ABHA, tele-obstetrics, mobile diagnostics and district-focused funding.

topics.t: Mental health, health accounts, education reports
p: Supreme Court task force on student mental health: 75% of mental illness begins before 24; student suicides were 7.6% of suicides (NCRB 2022); 65% of surveyed institutions have no mental health provider.
National Health Accounts 2022-23: government health spending 1.43% of GDP (from 1.15%); out-of-pocket share down from 64.2% to 43.4%; social security spending 9.9%.
Parliamentary Committee on teacher education (380th report): ITEP in premier institutions, Rs 9,195 crore plan for 613 DIETs, fill faculty posts.
Committee on higher education: raise public spending to 6% of GDP (now about 4.12%), publish AISHE data on time, notify all 20 Institutes of Eminence (12 done), strengthen state universities.

Supreme Court (Articles 32 and 142): trafficking is an assault on constitutional dignity rooted in Article 23. Consent separates trafficking from voluntary adult sex work. Elements: act, means, exploitation (Palermo Protocol, 2000).
NCRB 2024: 6,018 trafficking victims, including 2,297 children. BNSS makes trafficking cognizable and non-bailable; BNS Sections 143-144 define it; ITPA 1956 and the NIA are other pieces.
UNHCR Global Trends 2025: 117.8 million forcibly displaced, the first fall in a decade; Rohingya are the largest stateless group, 22,700 in India.
UNHCR (1950, Geneva; Nobel 1954 and 1981) works under the 1951 Convention and 1967 Protocol (non-refoulement). India is not a party and handles refugees case by case.
NITI Aayog's 10-year roadmap targets a 120-150 billion dollar domestic value chain by 2035 and a top-three place in advanced packaging and OSAT.

Five pillars: Pioneering (research and IP), Policy and Investment (135-180 billion dollars, a nodal agency, single window, outcome-linked incentives), Production (wafer fab, packaging, materials, secure manufacturing), People (talent pyramid), Partnerships (US, Japan, EU, Korea).
India has about 20% of the world's chip design workforce and 13 approved projects; Semicon India has drawn about Rs 1.6 trillion; the market may reach 100-110 billion dollars by 2030.
Challenges: dependence on China for silicon, germanium and gallium, over 5 billion dollars for a modern fab, talent, water and power needs, and a 4-5 year build time.
Tools: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, SPECS (25% capex support), DLI and PLI schemes, state policies such as Gujarat's.
Synthetic biology builds or redesigns whole genomes, unlike genome editing that makes small changes; uses range from cell therapy to biodegradable plastics; risks are biosafety and biosecurity.

IMI-resistant mustard hybrids, bred by mutation breeding, tolerate imidazolinone herbicides and help control the parasitic weed Orobanche; India imported about 16 million tonnes of edible oil (Rs 1.6 lakh crore) in 2024-25.
ICAR-IIOR developed a biopolymer smart seed coating; SkyCast (fog and wind sensing at Delhi airport) made India the 19th country with such a system.
JWST detected methane on interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS. IIT Madras built ANCHOR, a detailed 3D atlas of the human brainstem.
Fibre-optic drones resist jamming; BGP hijacking misdirects internet traffic; the UN adopted a new HIV declaration with 95-95-95 goals for 2030.

topics.t: Harappan artefacts and the Dancing Girl
p: NCERT changed and then restored the original picture of the Harappan 'Dancing Girl' in a Class 9 textbook.
The bronze figurine from Mohenjo-daro (about 2600-1900 BCE) was found in 1926 in digs led by John Marshall; it is in the National Museum, Delhi.

Other finds: the steatite Priest-King, the Pashupati seal, mother goddess terracottas, fire altars (Kalibangan, Lothal), pictographic seals in boustrophedon script (still undeciphered), stone weights, carnelian beads (Chanhudaro, Lothal) and a game board at Dholavira.
Harappans worked copper and made bronze by adding tin.
A national survey under the mission has mapped over 1 crore manuscripts. It was announced in Budget 2025-26 with Rs 491.66 crore for 2025-2031, as a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Culture.
It replaces the National Mission for Manuscripts (2003). Parts: Manuscript Resource Centres, Conservation Centres and a National Digital Repository (Kriti Sampada, Manus Granthavali software).
A manuscript is a handwritten work at least 75 years old; the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act 1972 bars their export except by the Centre. India has an estimated 5 million.
UNESCO Memory of the World entries from India include the Rigveda (2007), Gilgit Manuscripts (2017), and the Natyashastra and Bhagavad Gita (2025).
GI tags: Bhagaiya silk, Kuchai tussar silk, Munda jewellery and bamboo craft (Jharkhand); Khurasani Imli, the baobab fruit, of Mandu, Madhya Pradesh.
India and China are talking about a joint UNESCO nomination for Xuanzang's (Hiuen Tsang) travelogue; he spent 16 years in India, studied under Shilabhadra at Nalanda and visited Harsha's court.
Udant Martand (Calcutta, 1826, editor Jugal Kishore Shukla) was the first Hindi newspaper; Hindi Journalism Day is on 30 May.
Sangeet Natak Akademi: set up 1953, apex body for performing arts, a society under the Ministry of Culture.
Gallantry awards: wartime Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra (1950); peacetime Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra (1952, renamed 1967).

topics.t: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY reaches every State
p: West Bengal joined, so PM-JAY now covers the whole country.

Launched in September 2018 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme run by the National Health Authority; cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year, cashless, from Day One for pre-existing diseases, with 1,961 packages in 27 specialities.
Covers 12 crore poorer families (about 55 crore people), ASHA and Anganwadi workers and all senior citizens aged 70+ through Ayushman Vay Vandana.
Progress (Feb 2026): 43.52 crore cards, 36,229 hospitals (public and private), 11.69 crore admissions and Rs 1.73 lakh crore of treatment.
The other three pillars of Ayushman Bharat: Arogya Mandirs, the Digital Mission and PM-ABHIM.
